Answer.description: Result of a Question: a direct reply. Every claim must be backed by evidence.

answer.description: The direct reply to the Operator's question, in markdown
answer.title: Answer

Answer.title: Answer

Bill.description: A billed cluster's cloud bill beside its estimate; `note` says why there is none.
Bill.title: Bill

CheckResult.description:
Result of a scheduled Check: does what the Operator wrote hold right now?
Every claim must be backed by evidence.

passed.description: true only when the evidence shows the Check holds; false when it doesn't, or when you couldn't tell (a tool failed, a target is missing)
passed.title: Passed

report.description: Required when passed is false, empty when true: the failure investigated like an alert

summary.description: One or two sentences: what holds, or what doesn't
summary.title: Summary

CheckResult.title: CheckResult

finding.description: What it showed, quoted or summarized, one line
finding.title: Finding

link.description: A link a tool returned that opens this evidence (e.g. from a generate_deeplink tool), copied exactly. Never build or edit one.
link.title: Link

source.description: The one tool that produced it, exactly as named in your tools, e.g. kubernetes_pod_logs. No arguments and no second tool: say which pod or query in the finding, and give each tool its own Evidence.
source.title: Source

InvestigationPage.description:
One Investigation in full: its Report, Answer or Check verdict as fields (the
app shows each as text), what waits for a decision, and what it did.
InvestigationPage.title: InvestigationPage

JiraState.description:
The Contract's Jira project for this Report (slice 11.5b): its issue once filed,
who is filing it while there is none yet, or nothing: it can be filed.
JiraState.title: JiraState

KillSwitch.description: A Contract's Kill switch (slice 11.2a): who turned it on, and when.
KillSwitch.title: KillSwitch

TriageReport.description: Result of investigating one alert group. Every claim must be backed by evidence.

category.description: Why it broke, not how it fails. bad_rollout: a new revision broke a workload whose earlier revision worked, including a rollout of another workload the alerting one depends on (wins over the other classes). dependency_failure: something it depends on is failing, with no rollout to blame. bad_config: wrong or missing config, command or probe. app_error: bug in the code, including memory leaks. resource_limits: limits too low for a healthy workload. image_unavailable: tag or registry problem. capacity: the cluster can't fit the workload.
category.title: Category

confidence.description: high: direct evidence (e.g. the error in logs); low: inferred
confidence.title: Confidence

probable_root_cause.description: Why it broke, with the deciding facts from the evidence: the value, limit, version, revision or time that proves it (e.g. memory limit 64Mi against a heap that needs about 200Mi), not only a summary of the change
probable_root_cause.title: Probable Root Cause

runbook.description: Runbook name used, if one matched
runbook.title: Runbook

summary.description: One or two sentences an on-call engineer reads first
summary.title: Summary

TriageReport.title: TriageReport

get.description: What to look at now in this Contract, most urgent first (slice 11.4).

delete.description: The only way a Kill switch goes off: the Operator, in the console.

post.description:
Approve or reject every Proposed action of the pause the page showed, as
Slack's buttons do (409 while the Kill switch is on, for an approval).
Right, or wrong with what was wrong: the agent drafts a Teaching from it.
The Report into the Contract's Jira project, once.

The token page's: the identity and the console's own page only, since it is
what earns the cookie every other call needs.
